DoD 1 — the authenticated post-verification finalization path.

ORDERING. `finalizeVerifiedAttempt` calls `verifiedReceipt` FIRST — `readStoredReceipt` re-decodes/re-encodes/byte-compares — and returns before any release could be attempted when the receipt is absent, unreadable or foreign. Only then does it select the attempt, re-read the sources and invoke `recordAttemptRelease`. Because the receipt now exists, the binding `recordAttemptRelease` composes internally carries a NON-NULL receipt, so the RELEASED row and the receipt-bearing binding co-occur in one call. No back-fill.

REAL COMMAND PATH. Wired into the registered `foundation.verification` async entry (`daemon-foundation-verification-command.ts`, after `service.verify` succeeds). It is ADVISORY there for the same reason the live dispatch path's release is: the receipt is already durable and IS the command's answer, so a not-yet-finalizable attempt must not retract it; a later replay of the same command finalizes idempotently.

STRICT RE-READS, each through its owning producer: attempt record (`readFoundationAttemptRecord`), activation (`durableActivation`), receipt (`readStoredReceipt`), journal (`readCurrentAttemptJournal`), safe boundary (`deriveSafeBoundary` then `readCurrentSafeBoundaryObservation`), terminal effects/resources (`deriveReleaseTerminal`), scheduler nine-key handoff (`deriveSchedulerHandoff`, built and DISCARDED — recordAttemptRelease builds its own).

MEASURED FINDING that changed the design: the safe-boundary observation is WRITTEN by the release path itself (`deriveSafeBoundary` -> `recordSafeBoundaryObservation`), so a lookup run before it reports ABSENT for an attempt whose run the host recorded perfectly well. The service therefore asks the producer first (replay-idempotent on this bound attempt's own decision key, so the release below replays that exact row) and only then re-reads by attempt.

IDENTITIES ONLY. `admitFinalizationRequest` is exact-arity over `Reflect.ownKeys` (blind-spot of `Object.keys` on a non-enumerable smuggled key, per the a20e8ef6 gotcha). Allow-list = {attemptAggregateId, verificationId}. Server supplies commandId/correlationId/principalId/projectId.

implementationPlan.description:
The co-occurring durable state — DoD 2.
The successful path leaves APPEND-ONLY durable state from which BOTH can be re-read: ONE RELEASED attempt row AND ONE CURRENT core `{digest, ref}` handoff binding WITH A NON-NULL, BYTE-VERIFIED RECEIPT. The co-occurrence is the deliverable — either alone is the state today's ordering already produces.
RECEIPT FIELDS DO TWO DIFFERENT JOBS AND MUST NOT COLLAPSE: core `receiptRef` NAMES the verified `verificationId`; `receiptSha256` REMAINS PINNED for DRIFT DETECTION. Collapsing them into one field silently removes drift detection while every existing test still passes — assert both independently.
KEEP THE TWO HANDOFFS DISTINCT (rail 1): scheduler's NINE-key `ReleaseHandoff` and core's TWO-key `ExpansionHandoffBinding` `{digest, ref}`. NEVER derive one by shape-casting the other. They share the word "handoff" and nothing else — different arity, different owner, different consumer.
REPLAYS ARE IDEMPOTENT: they neither OVERWRITE the first release nor CREATE CONFLICTING BINDINGS. Assert EXACT RAW ROW COUNTS on both aggregates — a state-only assertion cannot see a second binding, and a second binding is precisely what "conflicting" means here.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 2 — the co-occurring durable state. Delivered by ORDERING, not by a new writer.

CO-OCCURRENCE. Arm "RELEASED: a release row and a receipt-bearing binding co-occur" re-reads BOTH from durable bytes after one finalization: `readAttemptRelease` gives `outcome/attemptState = "RELEASED"` and `reason = "WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE"`, and `readReleaseHandoffBinding` gives a binding whose `receipt` is NON-NULL. The served arm proves the same pair through the registered handler and re-reads it from a FRESH store handle after the provider closed.

WHY IT WORKS WITHOUT PATCHING. `recordAttemptRelease` already composes the core binding at attempt-release-disposition.ts:222 via `deriveHandoffBinding` -> `recordReleaseHandoffBinding` -> `resolveAttemptReceipt`. That scan finds the receipt only if one already exists — which is precisely what the pre-verification ordering guaranteed it would not. Running the same writer AFTER the receipt makes `receipt` non-null on the first and only binding. No back-fill, no second write path.

TWO FIELDS, TWO JOBS, asserted independently:
  `binding.receipt.verificationId` === "verification-finalize-1"  (NAMES the verified verification)
  `binding.receipt.receiptSha256` === the seeded sha              (PINNED for drift detection)
  plus `receiptSha256 !== verificationId`, so a collapse of the two fields into one reddens this arm.
`readReleaseHandoffBinding`'s `reReadReceipt` re-reads the row and refuses RELEASE_HANDOFF_BINDING_RECEIPT_DRIFT when the stored sha stops matching — that drift check is what the pin buys, and it is unreachable if the fields collapse.

TWO HANDOFFS KEPT DISTINCT (rail 1). Asserted: `Object.keys(binding.handoff).sort()` === ["digest","ref"] and `handoff.ref !== handoff.digest`. The scheduler's nine-key `ReleaseHandoff` is built by `deriveSchedulerHandoff` and DISCARDED by the finalization — `recordAttemptRelease` builds its own from the same durable facts, so nothing composed in this module reaches the kernel as authority. Neither object is ever shape-cast from the other.

IDEMPOTENT REPLAYS, on EXACT RAW ROW COUNTS (not state assertions):
  first  finalization -> outcome RELEASED, rawCounts {bindings: 1, releases: 1}
  second finalization -> outcome NO_OP,    rawCounts {bindings: 1, releases: 1}  (unchanged)
  and `second.release.outcome` is still "RELEASED" — the standing row, not a new truth.
`rawCounts` counts events directly on `deriveReleaseHandoffAggregateId(...)` and `deriveAttemptReleaseAggregateId(...)`, so a SECOND binding would redden it where a state-only read could not see one. `commitRelease` pins expectedVersion 0; `recordReleaseHandoffBinding` answers from the standing row on identical re-derived bytes.

APPEND-ONLY preserved: no update, no delete, no history rewrite anywhere on this path.

implementationPlan.description:
The strict safe-boundary lookup — DoD 3, a real gap rather than a nicety: the safe-boundary event DOES carry `observationRef`, but the release carrier DISCARDS it and no attempt-keyed current selector exists.
Expose a strict project+attempt CURRENT safe-boundary lookup returning the PRODUCER-OWNED `observationRef`. Its shape is tightly constrained and each constraint prevents a specific failure:
  - SCAN ITS OWN EVENT VOCABULARY under ONE HORIZON — not a global scan, and not another module's vocabulary.
  - DELEGATE FINAL VALIDATION TO `readSafeBoundaryObservation`. This is what stops a SECOND, DIVERGENT definition of "a valid observation" existing; two validators drift and then disagree about the same row.
  - NEVER EXPORT OR DUPLICATE THE PRIVATE REF HASH. Duplicating it is how the second definition gets created.
  - NEVER TRUST SCANNED BYTES AS THE ANSWER. The scan LOCATES; the delegate DECIDES.
The horizon is AGGREGATE-SCOPED, not global: a global horizon check moves on any unrelated write and would refuse nearly every finalization on a busy daemon — green in a quiet test, useless in production.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 3 — `readCurrentSafeBoundaryObservation` in `attempt-safe-boundary-lookup.ts` (177 lines). TDD: written RED first (`Cannot find module './attempt-safe-boundary-lookup.js'`), then green — 9 arms, all passing.

THE GAP, RE-MEASURED: safe-boundary-observation.ts:184 derives `observationRef` and :203 writes it as the event id, but attempt-release-boundary.ts:97-99 keeps only `safeBoundaryObserved`, and `readSafeBoundaryObservation` is ref-keyed (:236-242). No attempt-keyed selector existed.

SCAN ITS OWN VOCABULARY. Scans `SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION_EVENT_TYPE` via `readEventsByTypeAfter` — not a global event walk. I EXPORTED that one constant from safe-boundary-observation.ts (a two-line addition beside the private literal) rather than restating "SafeBoundaryObserved" here, so the two modules cannot drift into two names for one stream. The REF and AGGREGATE DOMAINS and `digestOf` remain module-private to the producer, so the private ref hash is neither exported nor duplicated.

ONE HORIZON, AND IT BOUNDS RATHER THAN GUARDS. `store.readEventHorizon()` is captured once and the walk stops at `event.globalPosition > horizon`, so concurrent writes cannot lengthen the walk or make "current" depend on when the loop finished. There is deliberately NO global re-check afterwards — that would move on any unrelated write and refuse nearly every lookup on a live daemon. The aggregate-scoped guard is the delegate's own read of the observation aggregate; the finalization's own guard is the attempt's activation+dispatch versions.

THE SCAN LOCATES; THE DELEGATE DECIDES. `locatorOf` takes exactly ONE field out of scanned bytes — `observationRef` — and reads `attemptRef` only to decide whether the row points at the asked-for attempt. Everything else is `readSafeBoundaryObservation`'s: validity, byte-agreement, and PROJECT OWNERSHIP. The answer's `observationRef` is read off `read.observation.observationRef` (the DELEGATE'S certified field), never off the scanned payload.

DELIBERATE DESIGN CALL A REVIEWER WILL ASK ABOUT: the scan does NOT filter by projectId. Filtering there would move ownership into this module and make the delegate's PROJECT_MISMATCH arm unreachable — a strictness never exercised is one that can be deleted without a red test. So arm "carries the delegate's own PROJECT_MISMATCH refusal rather than deciding it" queries a foreign project and asserts `source == {code: "SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION_ABSENT", layer: "DAEMON_SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION"}`. A build that answered from scanned bytes returns the foreign observation and reddens exactly that arm — this is the DoD-3 delegation drill's target.

CLOSED VOCABULARY: 4 codes, ABSENT and UNRESOLVED kept distinct (an unobserved attempt and a row that will not validate demand opposite repairs). Store failure is SCAN_UNREADABLE, never an absence — asserted with a store whose `readEventsByTypeAfter` throws.

MEASURED FACT worth keeping: the producer pins expectedVersion 0 on a ref-derived aggregate, so a same-key re-observation REPLAYS and a DIFFERENT-key one is refused SAFE_BOUNDARY_COMMIT_CONFLICT / EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT. Either way exactly ONE raw row stands — asserted directly.

Focused gate: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 9 passed (9)`.

implementationPlan.description:
The refusal roster and the four distinct outcomes — DoD 4.
Every missing journal/receipt/context/boundary/resource/terminal/release fact, foreign or stale identity, malformed or unreadable row, conflicting retry, and MOVED HORIZON returns an EXACT STABLE WRAPPER CODE PLUS THE SOURCE'S CODE AND LAYER, and CREATES NO NEW RELEASE AUTHORITY. The wrapper says which stage refused; the source says why — flattening them loses the distinction between "the journal is unreadable" and "finalization refused".
FOUR OUTCOMES ASSERTED AS DISTINCT: DRAINING, NO_OP, RELEASED, and BINDING-WRITTEN-BUT-RELEASE-REFUSED.
THAT FOURTH IS THE SUBTLE ONE AND IS EXACTLY WHAT TODAY'S ORDERING PRODUCES — the core binding is written before the kernel while the release refuses — so it must be a first-class outcome with its own assertion, not folded into a generic refusal. A row that treats it as "just a refusal" cannot tell an operator that a binding is sitting there without a release.
NO NEW RELEASE AUTHORITY ON ANY REFUSAL PATH: assert the absence, not merely the refusal. Rail 0's un-upgradeable-DRAINING hazard is precisely a refusal path that wrote something.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 4 — refusal roster + four distinct outcomes. Focused gate: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 19 passed (19)`.

WRAPPER + SOURCE, never flattened. Refusal shape is `{code, layer: "DAEMON_ATTEMPT_FINALIZATION", ok:false, source: {code, layer} | null}`. `sourceOf` reads `layer` OR `refusedBy` (producers on this lane spell it both ways; reading only one would answer "UNKNOWN" for half the roster and make attribution untestable). `source` is null ONLY when our own admission declined and nothing upstream was consulted.

ROSTER — each arm asserts the EXACT wrapper AND the source's own code+layer, plus rawCounts {bindings:0, releases:0}:
- receipt ABSENT      -> RECEIPT_UNVERIFIED  + FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT_ABSENT @ DAEMON_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT
- receipt bytes drift -> RECEIPT_UNVERIFIED  + FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT_UNREADABLE @ DAEMON_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT
- foreign identity    -> RECEIPT_FOREIGN     + ..._RECEIPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH @ DAEMON_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT
- attempt absent      -> ATTEMPT_UNREADABLE  + FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_ABSENT @ DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT
- journal absent      -> JOURNAL_UNRESOLVED  + JOURNAL_RECORD_ABSENT @ DAEMON_JOURNAL_APPEND
- no provider run     -> BOUNDARY_UNRESOLVED + SAFE_BOUNDARY_RUN_UNREADABLE @ DAEMON_SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION
- movable resources   -> HANDOFF_UNRESOLVED  + RELEASE_HANDOFF_SOURCE_STALE (the builder's own layer)
- conflicting retry   -> RELEASE_REFUSED     + RELEASE_HANDOFF_BINDING_RECEIPT_AMBIGUOUS @ DAEMON_RELEASE_HANDOFF
- moved horizon       -> HORIZON_MOVED (our own; source null)
- malformed payload   -> REQUEST_MALFORMED (our own; source null); 8 forbidden keys swept and the sweep count asserted nonzero
Two arms explicitly assert `source.layer !== ATTEMPT_FINALIZATION_LAYER` — the restamp drill's target.

FOUR OUTCOMES, EACH ITS OWN ARM:
- RELEASED  — release row + receipt-bearing binding, rawCounts {1,1}
- DRAINING  — UNOBSERVED exit with the RESOURCE half of terminality only; a row IS written and records DRAINING, resumable false, rawCounts {1,1}
- NO_OP     — replay; rawCounts unchanged at {1,1}; the standing row still records RELEASED
- BINDING_WRITTEN_RELEASE_REFUSED — a store refusing ONLY the release aggregate's commit; ok:true, release null, binding non-null with receipt, releaseRefusal {ATTEMPT_RELEASE_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE @ DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RELEASE}, rawCounts {bindings:1, releases:0}
The fourth is claimed ONLY when `readAttemptRelease` answers ATTEMPT_RELEASE_RECORD_ABSENT, so a refusal that somehow left a row behind stays a refusal. That is how "no new release authority on a refusal path" is asserted rather than assumed.

NEW MEASURED FACT: with the terminal ledgers unwritten the deferral happens at the SERVER-BUILT HANDOFF (RELEASE_HANDOFF_SOURCE_STALE), one stage ABOVE the resource fence — zero rows on either aggregate, so rail 0's un-upgradeable-DRAINING hazard closes even earlier than the fence alone would close it.
